children: META hit a 52-week high near $779.82 after Meta Connect 2026. Company unveiled Muse Charm wearable, new Ray-Ban VR glasses, 100+ AI glass styles planned and a $1,299 VR device.
Analysts raised Meta Platforms (META) price targets after Meta Connect 2026: Citizens $885, JPMorgan $920, KeyBanc $900, Cantor $860; Morgan Stanley and Mizuho kept Overweight/Outperform ratings.
Meta Platforms (META) is developing Muse with a free-and-paid model and a planned transaction fee. Traders should note heavy AI and data center investment and pressure on cash flow and debt.
Meta (META) launched Muse, a personal AI agent aimed at boosting user productivity. Release was delayed to add security measures and address safety concerns before public rollout.
Meta (META) linked Muse to Instacart and Expedia, enabling direct e-commerce and travel-booking flows via Muse interfaces, expanding Muse-driven shopping and reservation functionality.
META added retail partners—Walmart, Best Buy, Sephora, Wayfair, Dick's Sporting Goods, Gap—enabling Muse voice shopping and appointment features; Amazon not listed.
Meta (META) unveiled Horizon Create (mobile) and Horizon Studio (browser/PC) — generative AI tools for game prototyping. Assets and projects sync across platforms. Early access via waitlist.
Meta Platforms (META) may combine AI, hardware and user data to push features across 3.6 billion users. Potential interfaces cited: Muse and smart glasses enabling fast app and device rollouts.
Traders watch Meta (META) for Muse adoption, user engagement, and proof AI ties into Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp data and future hardware; Apple noted as a potential rival.
META launched Meta One subscriptions: consumer plans $2.99–$19.99/mo, business/creator tiers $14.99–$49.99/mo, plus Expert $149/mo and Max $499/mo; full suite now global.
